description:
# Jacques Viéville Tarot (Paris, c. 1650)

## At a glance

One of the **three oldest surviving named Tarots de Marseille-family decks**, printed in Paris around 1650 by the *maître-cartier* **Jacques Viéville** — a near-contemporary of **Jean Noblet** (whose deck this library also holds). The single known copy is at the **Bibliothèque nationale de France** and is on **Gallica** (ark:/12148/btv1b10510963k). The woodcut is public domain; the BnF scan is free to reuse non-commercially with credit, and commercial reuse needs a BnF licence. Its 78 woodcut cards are shown here from the BnF scan, at high resolution.

## Why it matters — the road not taken

Viéville's pack is the great **outlier** of the early Parisian tarots. Where Noblet sits squarely in the **C-order (Marseille)** line that became standard, Viéville's trump imagery leans toward the **Eastern/Belgian** branch: its figures face the other way, several trumps (the Popess, the Sun, the World, the Star) carry markedly different designs, and the pack is a key witness to the family that later surfaces in the **Vandenborre / 'Tarot Flamand'** decks rather than the Marseille mainstream. It shows that c. 1650 Paris held *two* competing tarot patterns at once.

## What you're looking at

- **22 atouts (trumps):** 21 carry printed Roman numerals (read directly from the scans here) plus the unnumbered **Mat** (Fool).
- **56 suit cards:** four Italian suits — **Épées** (Swords), **Deniers** (Coins), **Bâtons** (Batons), **Coupes** (Cups) — each with King, Queen, Cavalier, Valet and ten pips.
- The even-numbered canvases of the BnF scan are the cards' **patterned backs**; only the faces are shown.

## Honesty notes

The trumps are identified by their **printed numerals AND their scenes** — and the two together reveal a key feature: the Viéville follows the older **Eastern trump order**, not the later Marseille standard. Here **Justice is VII, the Chariot VIII, Strength VIIII, and the Hermit XI** — exactly the cards the Marseille (Conver) sequence reorders. This non-standard order is itself the evidence for the deck's Eastern/Belgian-leaning lineage. Suit cards are shown in **BnF folio order**; courts are identified by figure, and **pip ranks are assigned by position and may warrant correction** — corrections welcome, as everywhere in this library.

## Game, not divination

Like Noblet, this is a **playing-and-trick-taking** pack from a century before tarot was attached to fortune-telling; no cartomantic meaning is native to it.

## Sources

BnF / Gallica (ark:/12148/btv1b10510963k), Source gallica.bnf.fr / Bibliothèque nationale de France; Thierry Depaulis on the early Parisian cartiers; Dummett, *The Game of Tarot*.

metadata._celestial_note: Viéville's Star = an astronomer with compasses; Moon = a woman with a spindle under a tree; Sun = a youth on horseback — celestial designs that diverge from the Marseille (Belgian-line). See research/cards/vieville-tarot.md.

sections.About: The mountebank at his table — the deck opens, as the Parisian pattern does, with the conjuror.
sections.Research note:
**What changed (vs. its parent):** Substantially the same subject and position as Marseille's I; the low trumps are the most shared territory between the two patterns [@web_th_french_connection]. 

*Sources:* [@dummett1980], [@web_pollett_vieville], [@web_th_french_connection].

*Full card-by-card research:* [research/cards/vieville-tarot.md](https://github.com/PlayfulProcess/recursive-tarot/blob/main/research/cards/vieville-tarot.md).
sections.Symbol: The conjurer/magician at his table — skill and dexterity made visible, the one who commands attention by manipulating what lies in plain sight.

sections.About: A seated, winged figure with the papal tiara — the Viéville's idiosyncratic Popess.
sections.Research note:
**What changed (vs. its parent):** Same trump *role* as Marseille's Papesse, but the figure's treatment is idiosyncratic; in the later Belgian descendants this slot is replaced entirely (by the "Spanish Captain" in Vandenborre), so the Papesse here marks Viéville as *earlier/more conservative* than the mature Belgian pattern [@web_th_spanish_captain; @web_th_french_connection]. 

*Sources:* [@web_pollett_vieville], [@web_th_spanish_captain].

*Full card-by-card research:* [research/cards/vieville-tarot.md](https://github.com/PlayfulProcess/recursive-tarot/blob/main/research/cards/vieville-tarot.md).
sections.Symbol: Winged crowned reader — spiritual knowledge in a form that transcends institutional religion, doctrine held by one who is neither nun nor pope but something between.

sections.About: Enthroned with the eagle shield and a cross-staff — the Empress.
sections.Research note:
**What changed (vs. its parent):** Broadly concordant with Marseille's Empress. 

*Sources:* [@web_pollett_vieville].

*Full card-by-card research:* [research/cards/vieville-tarot.md](https://github.com/PlayfulProcess/recursive-tarot/blob/main/research/cards/vieville-tarot.md).
sections.Symbol: Winged empress with eagle-shield — sovereignty that reaches beyond earthly bounds, the union of imperial command and divine protection.

sections.About: The crowned Emperor.
sections.Research note:
**What changed (vs. its parent):** Broadly concordant with Marseille's Emperor (replaced by "Bacus" in the later Belgian pattern, but not here) [@web_th_bodet]. 

*Sources:* [@web_pollett_vieville], [@web_th_bodet].

*Full card-by-card research:* [research/cards/vieville-tarot.md](https://github.com/PlayfulProcess/recursive-tarot/blob/main/research/cards/vieville-tarot.md).
sections.Symbol: Standing emperor in profile with orb and heraldic eagle — authority in motion, imperial command expressed through stance rather than throne.

sections.About: The Pope / Hierophant.
sections.Research note:
**What changed (vs. its parent):** Same role as Marseille's Pape; like the Papesse, this papal card survives in Viéville where the mature Belgian decks later swap it out [@web_th_french_connection; @web_th_bodet]. 

*Sources:* [@web_pollett_vieville].

*Full card-by-card research:* [research/cards/vieville-tarot.md](https://github.com/PlayfulProcess/recursive-tarot/blob/main/research/cards/vieville-tarot.md).
sections.Symbol: Enthroned pope between pillars with kneeling petitioners — hierarchical spiritual authority, the transmission of sacred blessing through institutional form.

sections.About: The Lovers, under the radiant cupid.
sections.Research note:
**What changed (vs. its parent):** Concordant in subject with Marseille's L'Amoureux. 

*Sources:* [@web_pollett_vieville].

*Full card-by-card research:* [research/cards/vieville-tarot.md](https://github.com/PlayfulProcess/recursive-tarot/blob/main/research/cards/vieville-tarot.md).
sections.Symbol: Three young men under Cupid's arrow — love as a social bond and mutual pull, desire among companions rather than between suitor and beloved.

sections.About: Justice — sword and scales — numbered VII. The Viéville keeps the older Eastern order, where Justice sits at 7, not the Marseille-standard 8.
sections.Research note:
**What changed (vs. its parent):** **Order divergence.** Marseille places Justice at **VIII**; Viéville puts it at **VII**. The four-card virtue/Chariot/Hermit reshuffle (Justice VII, Chariot VIII, Force VIIII, Hermite XI) is a fingerprint of the non-Marseille, Bologna-derived lineage [@dummett1980; @web_th_french_connection; @web_aeclectic_vieville]. 

*Sources:* [@dummett1980], [@web_aeclectic_vieville].

*Full card-by-card research:* [research/cards/vieville-tarot.md](https://github.com/PlayfulProcess/recursive-tarot/blob/main/research/cards/vieville-tarot.md).
sections.Symbol: Winged Justice with sword and scales at position VII — the classical equilibrium between force and measure, placed ahead of the chariot of victory.

sections.About: The Chariot under its canopy, numbered VIII — the position the Marseille standard gives to Justice.
sections.Research note:
**What changed (vs. its parent):** **Order divergence** — VIII here is the slot Marseille gives to Justice. Plus an **iconographic divergence**: the human-faced/sphinx draught animals instead of Marseille's horses [@web_aeclectic_vieville]. 

*Sources:* [@web_aeclectic_vieville].

*Full card-by-card research:* [research/cards/vieville-tarot.md](https://github.com/PlayfulProcess/recursive-tarot/blob/main/research/cards/vieville-tarot.md).
sections.Symbol: Canopied throne with attendant crowned figures — triumph as ceremony and shelter rather than movement, the chariot reconceived as a seat of power.

sections.About: Strength — the figure mastering the lion — at VIIII (9), its Eastern-order position.
sections.Research note:
**What changed (vs. its parent):** **Order divergence.** Marseille places Strength at **XI**; Viéville at **VIIII**. (The much later Golden Dawn/RWS swap is a *different*, third re-ordering; Viéville's is the older Belgian-line arrangement, unrelated to it) [@dummett1980; @web_aeclectic_vieville]. 

*Sources:* [@dummett1980], [@web_aeclectic_vieville].

*Full card-by-card research:* [research/cards/vieville-tarot.md](https://github.com/PlayfulProcess/recursive-tarot/blob/main/research/cards/vieville-tarot.md).
sections.Symbol: Plumed figure wrestling a lion at position IX — courage and mastery over instinct, force applied through skill rather than brute strength.

sections.About: The Wheel of Fortune.
sections.Research note:
**What changed (vs. its parent):** Concordant in position and subject with Marseille's X. 

*Sources:* [@web_pollett_vieville].

*Full card-by-card research:* [research/cards/vieville-tarot.md](https://github.com/PlayfulProcess/recursive-tarot/blob/main/research/cards/vieville-tarot.md).
sections.Symbol: The turning wheel of Fortune with crowned figure at apex — cyclical rise and fall, the mechanical inevitability of change.

sections.About: The Hermit, the cloaked old man — at XI, where the Marseille standard puts Strength.
sections.Research note:
**What changed (vs. its parent):** **Order divergence.** Marseille places the Hermit at **VIIII** and Strength at XI; Viéville reverses this (Force VIIII, Hermite XI), completing the four-card virtue reshuffle [@web_aeclectic_vieville; @dummett1980]. 

*Sources:* [@dummett1980], [@web_aeclectic_vieville].

*Full card-by-card research:* [research/cards/vieville-tarot.md](https://github.com/PlayfulProcess/recursive-tarot/blob/main/research/cards/vieville-tarot.md).
sections.Symbol: Bearded figure shrouded in a cloak at position XI — solitude and self-enclosure, wisdom that protects itself from exposure rather than illuminating outward.

sections.About: The Hanged Man — in the Viéville/Belgian line the figure hangs **right-side-up** (a key divergence from the Marseille, where he hangs by one ankle, inverted). [research 2026-06-13]
sections.Research note:
**What changed (vs. its parent):** **Posture divergence.** Marseille's Pendu hangs inverted by one ankle; the Viéville figure is **upright** — one of the deck's signature departures [@web_aeclectic_vieville]. 

*Sources:* [@web_aeclectic_vieville].

*Full card-by-card research:* [research/cards/vieville-tarot.md](https://github.com/PlayfulProcess/recursive-tarot/blob/main/research/cards/vieville-tarot.md).
sections.Symbol: Upright figure between two poles — a Hanged Man who stands, suggesting willing pause rather than enforced reversal, suspension without inversion.

sections.About: Death — the scything skeleton (the card itself is unnamed, as usual).
sections.Research note:
**What changed (vs. its parent):** Concordant — unnamed Death at XIII, shared with Marseille [@dummett1980]. 

*Sources:* [@dummett1980], [@web_pollett_vieville].

*Full card-by-card research:* [research/cards/vieville-tarot.md](https://github.com/PlayfulProcess/recursive-tarot/blob/main/research/cards/vieville-tarot.md).
sections.Symbol: Dancing skeleton with red scythe over severed limbs — Death as relentless motion, the harvest of all things already underway.

sections.About: Temperance, pouring between two vessels.
sections.Research note:
**What changed (vs. its parent):** Concordant with Marseille's Tempérance. 

*Sources:* [@web_pollett_vieville].

*Full card-by-card research:* [research/cards/vieville-tarot.md](https://github.com/PlayfulProcess/recursive-tarot/blob/main/research/cards/vieville-tarot.md).
sections.Symbol: Crowned woman with torch and vessel, FAMA banner — Temperance recast as the herald of fame, moderation as a public and proclaimed virtue.

sections.About: The Devil.
sections.Research note:
**What changed (vs. its parent):** Same role/position as Marseille's XV; treatment varies but the subject is shared. 

*Sources:* [@web_pollett_vieville].

*Full card-by-card research:* [research/cards/vieville-tarot.md](https://github.com/PlayfulProcess/recursive-tarot/blob/main/research/cards/vieville-tarot.md).
sections.Symbol: Hairy winged beast carrying human figures — the Devil as creature of capture, supernatural predation without the contractual chains of later traditions.

sections.About: La Foudre — in the Viéville pack a **tree** struck by fire/hail with a shepherd figure beneath, NOT the Marseille struck **tower** (despite the 'Maison-Dieu' label). A signature marker of the Rouen-Brussels/Belgian line. [research 2026-06-13]
sections.Research note:
**What changed (vs. its parent):** **The signature divergence.** Marseille's XVI is *La Maison-Dieu*, a **tower struck by celestial fire**, figures tumbling. Viéville substitutes a **tree** and a **shepherd** under a rain of fire — a tree, not a tower [@web_th_rouen_bruxelles; @web_belgian_wp]. (The grammar's card text still gives the Marseille "tower struck and falling" reading — flagged for correction.). 

*Sources:* [@web_belgian_wp], [@web_th_french_connection], [@web_th_rouen_bruxelles].

*Full card-by-card research:* [research/cards/vieville-tarot.md](https://github.com/PlayfulProcess/recursive-tarot/blob/main/research/cards/vieville-tarot.md).
sections.Symbol: Tree struck by heavenly disc, drops falling, two witnesses below — the cosmic blow falls on natural growth rather than human construction, ruin without architectural hubris.

sections.About: The Star.
sections.Research note:
**What changed (vs. its parent):** **Iconographic divergence.** Marseille's Star is a **kneeling woman pouring water** from two ewers under a great star. Viéville shows instead a **standing astronomer measuring with compasses** — a learned, not a pastoral/nude, figure [@web_tarotforum_vieville_sms; @web_th_celestial]. 

*Sources:* [@web_tarotforum_vieville_sms], [@web_th_celestial].

*Full card-by-card research:* [research/cards/vieville-tarot.md](https://github.com/PlayfulProcess/recursive-tarot/blob/main/research/cards/vieville-tarot.md).
sections.Symbol: Bearded man with plant branch reaching toward a star — the Star as an object of contemplation and study, celestial guidance mediated through learning rather than devotion.

sections.About: The Moon.
sections.Research note:
**What changed (vs. its parent):** **Iconographic divergence.** Marseille's Moon shows two towers, two dogs/wolves baying, and a crayfish in a pool. Viéville shows a **spinning woman** — an image Tarot Heritage traces to a **Bolognese Sun card**, transferred onto the Viéville *Moon* (concrete support for the Bologna ancestry Dummett posits) [@web_th_celestial; @dummett1980]. 

*Sources:* [@web_tarotforum_vieville_sms], [@web_th_celestial].

*Full card-by-card research:* [research/cards/vieville-tarot.md](https://github.com/PlayfulProcess/recursive-tarot/blob/main/research/cards/vieville-tarot.md).
sections.Symbol: Full moon above a spinning woman and tree — the Moon as domestic timekeeper, lunation governing craft and feminine labor within the household.

sections.About: The Sun, with figures beneath.
sections.Research note:
**What changed (vs. its parent):** **Iconographic divergence.** Marseille's Sun shows **two children** (twins) before a wall under a rayed sun. Viéville shows a **single horseman** — a different scene entirely [@web_tarotforum_vieville_sms; @web_th_french_connection]. 

*Sources:* [@web_tarotforum_vieville_sms], [@web_th_french_connection].

*Full card-by-card research:* [research/cards/vieville-tarot.md](https://github.com/PlayfulProcess/recursive-tarot/blob/main/research/cards/vieville-tarot.md).
sections.Symbol: Human-faced sun above a banner-carrying rider — the Sun as triumphant procession, solar glory made mobile through the figure of a herald on horseback.

sections.About: The Judgement — the angel and the rising dead.
sections.Research note:
**What changed (vs. its parent):** Broadly concordant with Marseille's Jugement in subject. 

*Sources:* [@web_pollett_vieville].

*Full card-by-card research:* [research/cards/vieville-tarot.md](https://github.com/PlayfulProcess/recursive-tarot/blob/main/research/cards/vieville-tarot.md).
sections.Symbol: Lute-playing putto above two kneeling men — the call to awakening sounded in music rather than a trumpet blast, the divine summons as melody.

sections.About: The World.
sections.Research note:
**What changed (vs. its parent):** **Iconographic divergence.** Marseille's World is a **dancing figure in a mandorla/wreath, ringed by the four living creatures** (man, lion, ox, eagle). The Viéville/Belgian-line World departs from this composition (the grammar records only "The World" and should be expanded once the BnF scan is described in detail) [@web_aeclectic_vieville; @web_th_french_connection]. 

*Sources:* [@web_aeclectic_vieville], [@web_th_french_connection].

*Full card-by-card research:* [research/cards/vieville-tarot.md](https://github.com/PlayfulProcess/recursive-tarot/blob/main/research/cards/vieville-tarot.md).

sections.What it is: The Épées (Swords) suit — King, Queen, Cavalier, Valet and ten pips.
sections.Symbol: Swords as the suit of thought, conflict, and discernment — mental clarity and its shadow, the blade that cuts clean and the blade that wounds.

sections.About: Roi of Coins, from the Viéville pack (BnF folio order).
sections.Symbol: Inscribed golden coin with verse — the king of coins as proclamation, a monetary emblem surrounded by rhetoric of public fame and civic cry.

sections.About: Reine of Coins, from the Viéville pack (BnF folio order).
sections.Symbol: Maker's S-scroll with 'IACQUE VIEVIL A PARIS' — the queen of coins as the artisan's signature, identity and ownership inscribed within the suit of wealth.

sections.About: Cavalier of Coins, from the Viéville pack (BnF folio order).

sections.About: Huit of Batons, from the Viéville pack (BnF folio order).
sections.Symbol: Eight batons in double-cross symmetry — the suit in its structured middle register, force organized through geometric pattern.

sections.About: Sept of Batons, from the Viéville pack (BnF folio order).
sections.Symbol: Seven batons in active imbalance — the suit in creative tension, the odd number that forces engagement rather than rest.

sections.About: Six of Batons, from the Viéville pack (BnF folio order).
sections.Symbol: Six batons in balanced arrangement — the suit at equilibrium, fire and growth in a moment of stable correspondence.

sections.About: Cinq of Batons, from the Viéville pack (BnF folio order).
sections.Symbol: Five batons with central dominance — contest and vitality, the suit at its most actively contested and energetic point.

sections.About: Quatre of Batons, from the Viéville pack (BnF folio order).
sections.Symbol: Four batons in square or cross — the suit in its most stable four-fold expression, a foundation of energy rather than a burst of it.

sections.About: Trois of Batons, from the Viéville pack (BnF folio order).
sections.Symbol: Three batons in triangular relation — the beginning of organized force, three points of energy defining direction and momentum.

sections.About: Deux of Batons, from the Viéville pack (BnF folio order).
sections.Symbol: Two batons in primary crossing — the first meeting of forces, the suit's energy at its most elemental dyadic form.

sections.About: As of Batons, from the Viéville pack (BnF folio order).
sections.Symbol: One baton as emblem — the undivided fire and creative force of the suit, energy before it divides into contest or purpose.

sections.What it is: The Bâtons (Batons) suit — King, Queen, Cavalier, Valet and ten pips.
sections.Symbol: Batons as the suit of fire, growth, and creative will — here rendered in bold red cylinders that suggest both the peasant's staff and the wand of creative authority.

sections.About: Roi of Cups, from the Viéville pack (BnF folio order).
sections.Symbol: Castle-chalice with multiple turrets — the king of cups as architectural vessel, emotional authority rendered as a structure both contained and towering.

sections.About: Reine of Cups, from the Viéville pack (BnF folio order).
sections.Symbol: Three cups with dragon heads and verse inscription — the queen of cups as a card that speaks, the emotional suit's feminine rank carrying the deck's riddling voice.

sections.About: Cavalier of Cups, from the Viéville pack (BnF folio order).
sections.Symbol: Three cups in leafy interlace — the cavalier of cups as abundance in motion, emotional generosity embedded in living ornament.

sections.About: Valet of Cups, from the Viéville pack (BnF folio order).
sections.Symbol: Valet of cups with baton — the page at the threshold between suits, youth in possession of an attribute that crosses the boundary between water and fire.

sections.About: Dix of Cups, from the Viéville pack (BnF folio order).
sections.Symbol: Ten cups in full field — emotional completion, the suit at its most abundant and encompassing expression.

sections.About: Neuf of Cups, from the Viéville pack (BnF folio order).
sections.Symbol: Nine cups approaching fullness — emotional near-fulfillment, the suit one step from its final expression.

sections.About: Huit of Cups, from the Viéville pack (BnF folio order).
sections.Symbol: Eight cups in balanced arrangement — emotional equilibrium at the suit's stable middle point, cups in structured correspondence.

sections.About: Sept of Cups, from the Viéville pack (BnF folio order).
sections.Symbol: Seven cups in asymmetric field — emotional multiplicity, the suit's energy distributed among seven distinct receptacles.

sections.About: Six of Cups, from the Viéville pack (BnF folio order).
sections.Symbol: Six cups in open arrangement — emotional balance and exchange, the suit at its most harmonious and mutually receptive point.

sections.About: Cinq of Cups, from the Viéville pack (BnF folio order).
sections.Symbol: Five cups with central emphasis — emotional asymmetry, the suit's odd-number tension concentrated around the question of what is held and what is spilled.

sections.About: Quatre of Cups, from the Viéville pack (BnF folio order).
sections.Symbol: Four cups in square arrangement — emotional stability and interiority, the suit's four-fold structure as a container rather than an overflow.

sections.About: Trois of Cups, from the Viéville pack (BnF folio order).
sections.Symbol: Three cups in triangular arrangement — the beginning of emotional community, three vessels sharing a common ornamental ground.

sections.About: Deux of Cups, from the Viéville pack (BnF folio order).
sections.Symbol: Two cups in vertical correspondence — the primal emotional dyad, two vessels in relation, the beginning of exchange and reciprocity.

sections.About: As of Cups, from the Viéville pack (BnF folio order).
sections.Symbol: One cup as emblem — the undivided emotional potential of the suit, receptivity and feeling held in their most essential and generative form.

sections.What it is: The Coupes (Cups) suit — King, Queen, Cavalier, Valet and ten pips.
sections.Symbol: Cups as the suit of emotion, reception, and inner life — here given an unusual ornamental depth and textual voice, the suit that in the Viéville speaks as well as holds.

sections.About: The unnumbered Fool, the wandering figure — placed last in the BnF scan.
sections.Symbol: Walking fool carrying a golden grail-cup — the Fool as a bearer of hidden treasure, wandering without social rank but freighted with extraordinary cargo.

sections.What it is: The 22 trumps (atouts) of the Viéville — 21 numbered cards plus the unnumbered Mat.
sections.Symbol: The twenty-two major arcana of the Viéville deck as a collective field — a map of the soul's journey expressed through the most iconographically divergent surviving Marseille variant.
